name: Pyth BTC/USD price volatility
description: Realized volatility of the Pyth Network BTC/USD aggregate price on the oracle lane, from the Hermes stream source pyth.hermes.btc-usd.price. Pyth publishes at roughly one hertz, so this identity samples the aggregate price one-second causal and converts consecutive samples to simple basis-point returns. volatility_bps_1s, volatility_bps_10s, volatility_bps_30s, volatility_bps_1m, volatility_bps_5m, and volatility_bps_15m are the root mean square of the one-second returns inside the trailing one, ten, thirty, sixty, three-hundred, and nine-hundred second windows. short_long_ratio is the one-second value divided by the fifteen-minute value; when both windows have zero root-mean-square volatility the ratio is defined as 1 (the micro convention) and regime is stable. Regime is contracting at or below 0.8, expanding at or above 1.2, and stable between those boundaries; the 0.8 and 1.2 boundaries are initial research thresholds that require empirical calibration. Any missing or stale one-second observation breaks continuity and restarts the fifteen-minute warm-up. This definition ships approved but refuse-closed today, on the same precedent as btc.pyth.oracle_reference: no processor consumes pyth.hermes.btc-usd.price on the oracle lane yet, so the identity publishes no ready values and refuses at start-up. It begins publishing once the Pyth Hermes stream is wired as a lane input (slice C4). Reads only Pyth and predicts nothing. Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
